title: Where Anomaly Meets Normality
description: An anomaly in physics is a law that holds classically but fails in the quantum world: a conserved charge that quietly is not. Where a defect touches ordinary space, such failures leak out - local violations the rest of physics must absorb. Unlocks the Local Law Violation.

puzzle.goal: Massless fermions have a chiral charge that the classical equations conserve exactly. Put them in parallel electric and magnetic fields and quantum effects break that conservation: chiral charge appears out of the vacuum at a rate set by the fine-structure constant through e², and by the fields' dot product. Write the source of chiral charge per unit volume, with ħ and c written out.
puzzle.name: Adler–Bell–Jackiw chiral anomaly
puzzle.lhs: pd ( ρ , t ) + div ( vec ( j ) )
puzzle.ask: In natural units (ħ = c = 1, e² = 4πα) the source is (2α/π)·E·B for parallel fields. Find it for the fields below.
puzzle.method: In a magnetic field the fermions fill Landau levels; the lowest one is chiral and one-dimensional. An electric field along B pumps states through it at a rate eE/2π per unit length, and the level holds eB/2π states per unit area.
